'''Vadim Anatolyevich Yankov''' ({{langx|ru|Вади́м Анато́льевич Янко́в}}; 1 February 1935 – 11 March 2024) was a Russian mathematician, philosopher, and [[political prisoner]].

In 1968, Yankov co-signed a {{ill|Letter of 99|lt=letter of 99 Soviet mathematicians|ru|Письмо девяноста девяти}} asking for the release of imprisoned mathematician [[Alexander Esenin-Volpin]].<ref name="letter-99">{{in lang|ru}} [http://www.math.ru/history/p99/index.htm Text of the letter]. math.ru. Retrieved 21 February 2014.</ref>

Shortly before the 1981 [[martial law in Poland|martial law crisis in Poland]], Yankov sent out a seven-page [[samizdat]] letter "A Letter to Russian Workers
about the Events in Poland". In it, he encouraged the Soviet working class to follow the example of [[Solidarity (Polish trade union)|Solidarity]], stressing social participation and non-violent protest.<ref>{{Cite journal| issn = 2000-2955| volume = IV| issue = 3| pages = 42–46| last = Ljunggren| first = Magnus| title = Memories of a Land in Stagnation| journal = Baltic Worlds| date = 2011 | url = https://balticworlds.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/10/BW-11.3.pdf}}</ref>{{rp|45–46}}

In 1982, he was arrested and charged with [[Anti-Soviet agitation|anti-Soviet agitation and propaganda]].<ref>{{in lang|ru}} http://www.memo.ru/history/DISS/chr/XTC65-13.htm</ref> He was sentenced in January 1983 to four years of [[Gulag|imprisonment]] and three years in [[exile|internal exile]]. He served his time in Dubravlag labor camp in [[Mordovia]], near [[Moscow]], and his exile in [[Buryatia]] in south-central Siberia. He was released in January 1987 and [[Rehabilitation (Soviet)|rehabilitated]] in 1991.<ref>{{in lang|ru}} http://lists.memo.ru/d38/f388.htm</ref> Yankov is featured as a prominent character in [[Levan Berdzenishvili]]'s novel ''Sacred Darkness'', describing their joint time in prison.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Berdzenishvili |first1=Levan |title=Sacred Darkness |date=2019 |publisher=Europa Editions |location=London }}</ref> 

After 1991, he taught mathematics and philosophy at the Department of Intellectual Systems at [[Russian State University for the Humanities]] in Moscow.

Yankov died on 11 March 2024, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite news |title=Умер диссидент и учёный Вадим Янков |url=https://www.svoboda.org/a/umer-dissident-i-uchyonyy-vadim-yankov/32858255.html |access-date=25 March 2024 |publisher=Svoboda |date=12 March 2024}}</ref>
